standard.title: Present media arts works
standard.description: present media arts works, using responsible media practices and considering potential relationships the work could create with audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can present media arts works to an audience (AC9AMA6P01). They have not yet made deliberate presentation decisions about distribution context, audience relationships, copyright/ICIP obligations, or evaluated how different presentation contexts change audience reception.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students present media arts works using responsible media practices and with deliberate consideration of how presentation choices shape audience relationships.

nodes.label: Applying responsible media practices in presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply copyright, ICIP and ethical obligations when presenting media arts works
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one responsible media practice obligation relevant to presenting own work; explain how it is applied in the presentation
nodes.typical_width: Apply copyright, ICIP and ethical obligations when presenting media arts works; explain specific decisions made to comply with responsible practice requirements
wider: Research copyright laws and ICIP rights relevant to specific content in own work — document how permission was obtained or why specific material was not included
Develop a presentation plan that explicitly addresses all responsible practice obligations before distribution — evaluate how responsible practice shaped presentation decisions
Investigate how media arts makers navigate copyright and ICIP obligations in professional distribution contexts — apply those practices to own work

response_modes.reason: Students commonly treat copyright and ICIP obligations as administrative hurdles rather than reasoned professional practice. Scaffolding the reasoning — what is the obligation, why does it exist, how does it apply to this specific content in this specific context — builds genuine understanding of responsible practice rather than compliance-as-checklist.

success_criteria: Identifies and applies at least one responsible practice obligation in presentation
Explains why the obligation exists and how it applies
Responsible practice is genuinely applied — not just acknowledged

nodes.label: Considering audience relationships in presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make deliberate presentation decisions that consider the potential relationship the work creates with the intended audience
nodes.minimum_width: Make at least one deliberate presentation decision (platform, timing, context) with an explicit consideration of the audience relationship it creates; explain the reasoning
nodes.typical_width: Plan presentation with deliberate consideration of audience relationships; reflect on how different presentation contexts affect interpretation and engagement; document reasoning
wider: Distribute a media arts work to a specific audience using appropriate platforms — evaluate how the distribution context shapes audience engagement and relationship
Present media arts works in multiple contexts (online platform, school exhibition, community screening) — evaluate how each context changes audience interpretation and response
Reflect on how relationships develop between media arts makers and audiences across a cohort — evaluate how shared or differentiated audience experiences change reception

response_modes.reason: Thinking deliberately about audience relationships in presentation — not just choosing a platform but reasoning through what relationship the presentation creates — is a production practice habit that develops through repeated consideration cycles. Students who present without this reasoning don't develop the audience-centred presentation thinking the descriptor requires.

success_criteria: Makes at least one presentation decision with explicit audience relationship reasoning
Explains how the presentation context shapes the audience relationship
Presentation is audience-centred — not just platform selection

nodes.label: Evaluating presentation and audience reception
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how presentation choices affected audience reception and what this reveals about the relationship between presentation context and meaning
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on how the chosen presentation context affected how audiences received the work; identify at least one thing that worked and one that would change
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the effectiveness of presentation choices across different audience contexts; reflect on the relationship between presentation decisions and audience reception; document how evaluation would inform future presentation
wider: Present the same work in different contexts and compare audience responses — evaluate how context changes what the work communicates and what relationship it creates
Collect audience feedback and evaluate the gap between intended and received meaning — develop criteria for evaluating presentation effectiveness
Evaluate how different audiences within the same cohort interpreted the work differently — analyse what the differences reveal about how media works create meaning

response_modes.reason: This node integrates responsible practice application (Node 1), audience relationship consideration (Node 2), and production work from C01/C02 into a complete evaluation of how a media arts work reached its audience. Students who can present but cannot evaluate the relationship between presentation choices and audience reception have not met the standard's full demand.

success_criteria: Reflects on how presentation context affected audience reception
Identifies at least one specific aspect that worked and one that would change
Evaluation addresses the relationship between presentation choice and audience reception
